blocks.text: `phase1_test_drive`, `phase1_live_drive` and `run_scenario` return a struct `res` and save the run in `work/results/<ID>_<date>_<time>.mat`. The most useful fields: `res.S` (all logged signals), `res.eval` (criteria), `res.ok`/`res.msg` (errors), `res.rtf` (speed) and `res.file` (saved log).

`plot_run` draws every logged signal of a run on six figure pages: **drive**, **tracks**, **battery**, **power**, **rc** and **nav**. It works for any saved run (live drive, test drive, scenarios); all six pages take about a minute.

plot_run(res)                                 % the run just finished
plot_run('L1')                                % newest live drive (also 'D1', 'S1', ... or a log name)
plot_run(res, 'Pages', {'drive', 'battery'})  % some pages only
plot_run(res, 'TimeRange', [200 236])         % zoom; the time axes of a page move together
plot_run(res, 'Save', true)                   % PNGs in work/reports/plots_<log name>/

items: Background bands on every time plot: **grey** = not armed (BOOT, SELFTEST, STANDBY), **yellow** = HOLD, **red** = ESTOP or FAULT.
A tile whose signals the run did not log, or that stay at zero in the chosen model variant, shows a note instead of an empty line.
Zoom and pan with the axes toolbar; all time plots of the page follow.

blocks.text: The figures below come from a 236 s live drive with the PS5 controller (log `L1_20261027_011510`): 141.7 m driven, top speed 2.0 m/s, no E-stop, no fault. The explanations say what each tile shows, what normal looks like and what this run shows.

blocks.caption: plot_run page drive: operator commands, speed and yaw-rate command vs response, path on the field and MCU mode.

items: **Operator commands:** throttle (CH2), steering (CH1) and the speed scale (CH7) as the MCU decoded them from the SBUS frames. Here the speed scale was 75 % from 20 s (L1) and 100 % from 212 s (R1).

**Forward speed:** MCU target = stick x speed scale x 2.0 m/s; MCU reference = the target after the acceleration ramp; actual = true speed of the robot. The actual speed should follow the reference within a fraction of a second. A lasting gap means slip, a torque limit (page 2) or a battery limit (page 3).

**Yaw rate:** the same for turning (+ = left), plus the gyro reading the MCU uses. In this run the gyro reading lags after hard turns and reads about -0.4 rad/s from 207 s while the robot drives straight; this is an open model issue (IMU model or gyro-bias correction) and goes with the IMU_FAULT warnings on page 5.

**Path:** true path, coloured by speed; green dot = start, red square = end. The dashed green line is the edge of the field map (60 x 60 m in world 1); red points are outside the map, as in the last 17 s of this run.
**MCU mode:** BOOT -> SELFTEST -> STANDBY within 1.1 s, MANUAL from arming (21.6 s) to the end. HOLD, ESTOP or FAULT would show here and as bands on all pages.

blocks.caption: plot_run page tracks: track speeds, motor speeds, torques and limits, slip and motor power.

items: **Left / right track speed:** MCU reference (from the speed and yaw-rate references), measured (motor encoder), true belt speed and true ground speed. Belt faster than ground = slip. Negative values on one side are pivot turns.
**Motor speed:** ESC setpoint (dashed) and actual motor speed in rpm; 2.0 m/s track speed is about 3,600 rpm.

**Motor torque:** actual torque, MCU feed-forward torque (dotted) and the MCU motoring limit (dashed, 16 N m; lower when the MCU derates). Torque sitting on the limit means the robot cannot follow the reference.

**Slip and traction control:** true slip = (belt - ground) / belt speed. Short spikes at low speed and in pivot turns are normal; long slip above about 0.2 while driving means poor traction. Traction factor 1 = no traction-control action.
**Motor DC power and losses:** electrical input of each drive (negative = regenerative braking) and the losses in motor, ESC and gearbox (dotted).

blocks.caption: plot_run page battery: SOC, pack voltage, current and power, energy breakdown, cells, BMS limits and remaining energy.

items: **State of charge:** true SOC, BMS estimate, BMS coulomb count and the value the MCU receives over CAN. The BMS estimate should stay within a few tenths of a percent of the truth. Here: 95.0 % -> 94.7 %.
**Pack voltage and current:** terminal voltage (truth and BMS) and pack current (+ = discharge). The voltage sags about 0.3 V at 45 A.
**Power:** pack power = traction (both motors) + LV electronics (about 60 W) + losses.

**Energy (cumulative):** energy out of the pack and where it went (traction, implement, LV electronics, losses). The title gives the total and the consumption per km: here 47.6 Wh, 336 Wh/km. Use it to compare drives, implements and soils.
**Cell voltages:** the 16 cell groups (thin grey) and the BMS minimum and maximum. A spread below about 10 mV means a balanced pack.
**Cell temperatures:** cells (thin), BMS maximum, pack air and ambient (45 degC in world 1).

**BMS current limits:** discharge limit (DCL, 300 A) and charge limit (CCL, 100 A); the pack current must stay below them. The BMS lowers them with the cell temperature, near the cell voltage limits and (discharge) at low SOC.
**Remaining energy and runtime:** BMS remaining energy (about 13 kWh) and the runtime at the present load (shown up to 24 h).

blocks.text: Page 4 - power: power electronics, safety chain and temperatures

blocks.caption: plot_run page power: low-voltage rails, HV bus, contactors and safety chain, conversion losses and temperatures.

items: **Low-voltage rails:** 24 V, 24 V implement, 12 V, 5 V and 3.3 V. A rail below its minimum sets the RAIL_UV bit (page 5).
**HV bus and rail currents:** HV bus and pack voltage; 24 V and 12 V rail currents (about 1 A and 3.4 A here).

**Contactors, safety chain and power flags:** one row per flag; a thick bar = true (green = normal, red = a problem flag, blue = information), a thin grey line = false. Normal driving: key on, K1 closed, BMS HV ready, MCU power ready, all rails OK, safety relay and both E-stop channels OK. The red mark at 0 s is the start-up.
**Conversion losses:** DC/DC converter, power distribution unit (PDU) and the two drives.
**Temperatures:** motor windings, housings and ESCs, enclosure (MCU) and ambient. Here the windings warmed from 45 degC to 53-56 degC in 4 minutes of driving.

blocks.text: Page 5 - rc: RC link and MCU health

blocks.caption: plot_run page rc: all RC channels, radio link, SBUS counters, MCU fault and warning bits, command source and ESC states.

items: **RC channels:** all 14 channels after SBUS decoding (-1 to 1 around each line). Sticks move continuously; switches show as steps: here CH6 arm at 21.6 s, CH7 speed scale steps and CH11 lift pulses (L2 / R2, no effect without an implement).

**Radio link quality and frame age:** link quality 0-1, lost single frames (red triangles; the simulated radio drops a few) and the age of the last good frame. Normal: below 30 ms. The MCU sets RC_LINK_LOST above 100 ms and stops the robot.
**SBUS counters:** frames accepted (here 16,821 in 236 s, one frame every 14 ms); frames rejected, frames skipped and MCU task overruns should stay at 0.

**MCU fault and warning bits:** only the bits that were set, by number and name (`docs/icd.md`). Orange = warning (condition present), red = fault (persisted or latched; stops or limits the robot). Here: start-up bits at 0 s (RC_LINK_LOST, RAIL_UV) and three short IMU_FAULT warnings at 214-225 s.
**Command source and ESC states:** command source 1 = RC after arming; both ESCs go READY -> OPERATION when armed. FAULT or STO here explains a robot that stops.

blocks.text: Page 6 - nav: navigation and vehicle dynamics

blocks.caption: plot_run page nav: navigation estimate vs truth, roll and pitch, accelerations, GNSS, navigation flags, slip and ground contact.

items: **Position estimate error and heading:** navigation estimate vs truth. In Phase 1 the navigation fusion does not run, so the position tile shows a note and only the true heading is drawn; Phase 2 runs show both.

**Roll and pitch:** true attitude, the MCU estimate and the terrain grade. The fast preset has a kinematic chassis (true roll and pitch stay 0); the MCU estimate shows about +2 / -2 deg from the IMU. Tilt warnings start at 22 deg.
**Body accelerations:** MCU acceleration reference, true forward and lateral acceleration, raw IMU x and y (they include a gravity part when the IMU is tilted).
**GNSS:** fix type (4 = RTK fixed, reached after 4 s here), satellites (28) and the reported horizontal accuracy.
**Navigation flags:** as on page 4. In Phase 1 only GNSS heading valid is true.

**Track slip and ground contact:** true slip (plus the estimate in Phase 2) and the normal force on each track (constant 16.1 kN with the kinematic chassis; it changes on slopes with `'Fidelity','full'`).

blocks.text: For your own plots: signals are grouped, for example `truth` (true vehicle motion), `telem` (MCU telemetry such as `mode`, `v_target`), `power_truth` (battery) and `drive_truth` (motors). Each signal has `.t` and `.v`.
MCU mode numbers in `S.telem.mode`: 0 BOOT, 1 SELFTEST, 2 STANDBY, 3 MANUAL, 4 HOLD, 5 AUTO_START, 6 AUTO, 7 CTRL_STOP, 8 ESTOP, 9 FAULT.
